title: Celebrate 90 Years of Mopar with a Special-Edition Charger Debut at SEMA

body_markdown:
Here’s an extra-credit contender for your next automotive trivia night competition: How and when did Chrysler create the term it uses to signify “genuine Chrysler parts and accessories?”


That would, of course, be “MOPAR,” or now Mopar, a portmanteau created in 1937 from “MOtor PARts,” which is being celebrated at this year’s Specialty Equipment Market Association annual trade show in Las Vegas.


Mopar has seldom let a public-relations opportunity pass by without a little mechanical exploitation, so you won’t be surprised that they are commemorating “90 Years of Mopar Passion, Performance and Personalization” with a “limited-production drop that combines unique styling, carbon-fiber details and functional performance enhancements to the all-wheel-drive Dodge muscle car.”


Stellantis


It salutes[the Charger](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/report-v-8-hellcat-charger-will-return-in-2028/) , the fourth time the model has been given a full Mopar treatment since 2011. We’d have to stop and ponder what those last three treatments were, though Mopar helpfully reminds us that they occurred in ’11, ’15 and ’23. This time, they are Mopar-ing the two-door Sixpack-powered, 420-horsepower Charger R/T, and the 550-horse Charger Scat Pack Plus. Both come with standard all-wheel-drive (and on-demand rear-wheel drive) and[twin-turbocharged 3.0-liter inline six-cylinder](https://www.hagerty.com/media/videos/can-dodges-six-cylinder-charger-beat-its-ev-brother-and-the-m2-cs/) engines.


Retail price for the package is $10,995. Production will be color-limited to a total of 270 units, with 90 vehicles offered in each of three exterior shades: Bludicrous, Diamond Black, or White Knuckle. (Is it just us, or does “Diamond Black” sound comparatively sub-passionate?)


Here’s what you get: A carbon-fiber front and rear splitter, a carbon-fiber hood with a functional scoop, plus a cold-air intake system, all with the Direct Connection branding. There’s also “unique bodyside and hood graphics,” a serialized Mopar ’27/Mopar 90th anniversary under-hood plaque mounted on a radiator panel, and a “unique interior badge on the dashboard.”


Dealers will begin taking orders in early January 2027, with production starting in the spring. If you live north of the border, get your order in quickly, as the U.S. gets 243 cars, while Canada gets just 27.


Despite the limited run, Darren Bradshaw, senior vice president of Stellantis parts and services for North America, nonetheless notes that, “The Mopar ’27 Dodge Charger showcases our passion for personalization and performance while celebrating nine decades of helping enthusiasts make their vehicles uniquely their own. Our latest special-edition, limited-build package delivers exclusive styling, premium materials and signature Mopar touches that celebrate the passion, performance and personalization enthusiasts have come to expect from Mopar.”
